description: We are a team of passionate minds eager to explore ideas, solve real-world challenges, and create meaningful solutions through the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We welcome motivated team members with skills in coding, AI/ML, data analysis, design, research, or presentation. Most importantly, we value creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to learn.
summary: AETHERHEART is a research-driven project that explores the scientific, historical and engineering significance of human-made hardware left across the Moon and Mars. We have compiled a detailed planetary hardware archive documenting spacecraft, rovers, landers, rocket stages, scientific instruments and mission debris, including their locations, masses, functions and present conditions. Beyond documenting these assets, our research examines how lunar and Martian environments affect materials over time, the decay of radioisotope power systems, and the potential of abandoned spacecraft materials for future in-situ resource utilization. We also investigate the importance of protecting historic landing sites from future mission activities. To turn this research into practical solutions, we propose four software tools: an interactive planetary hardware atlas, a heritage protection zone calculator, an ISRU resource valuation engine, and an AI-assisted change detection system. Our goal is to preserve humanity’s space heritage while supporting safer, more sustainable planetary exploration.
details:
AETHERHEART is a research-driven project documenting human-made hardware left on the Moon and Mars. It catalogues spacecraft, rovers, landers, rocket stages and mission debris, analysing their locations, functions, scientific contributions and current conditions.

Our project explores four innovative solutions: an interactive planetary hardware atlas, a heritage protection zone calculator, an ISRU resource valuation engine, and an AI-assisted surface change detection system. These aim to help locate planetary assets, protect historic landing sites, assess reusable materials and monitor changes on planetary surfaces.

By combining space science, engineering, geospatial analysis and artificial intelligence, AetherHeart views abandoned hardware not simply as debris, but as scientific records, historical landmarks and potential resources. Our goal is to encourage space education, preserve humanity’s space heritage and support more sustainable future exploration.
